verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: the remaining patches complete SQL:2011 features on top of the FOR PORTION OF core committed for v19. Three fixable design points remain open. standards-compat-1 asks how a PERIOD's hidden column behaves in pg_dump and psql. maintenance-fit-2 asks for one updated-columns set that includes the range column, and maintenance-fit-1 asks which `ForPortionOfState` fields triggers may rely on. Nobody reviewed these follow-on patches in the visible thread.

brief.title: UPDATE/DELETE FOR PORTION OF and follow-on temporal features
brief.problem: Users of temporal primary and foreign keys, released in v18, have no way to change only part of a row's application time. The author says temporal keys are hard to use without temporal DML. Temporal foreign keys also support only NO ACTION.
brief.proposed_design: `update` and `delete` accept `FOR PORTION OF col FROM x TO y` or `FOR PORTION OF col (expr)`. The executor narrows the matched row to the target and inserts up to two "temporal leftovers" for the untouched time, computed by new set-returning functions. Later patches expose the bounds to triggers and use them for temporal foreign key CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT and PERIOD DDL.
user_visible_surface: SQL syntax: `UPDATE/DELETE ... FOR PORTION OF range_column_name { FROM start TO end | (expression) }`; NULL bounds mean unbounded.
Functions `range_minus_multi(anyrange, anyrange)` and `multirange_minus_multi(anymultirange, anymultirange)`, both returning setof.
Leftover inserts fire INSERT row and statement triggers nested inside the UPDATE/DELETE triggers, and need no INSERT privilege.
C API: new `tg_temporal` field in `TriggerData`, pointing to `ForPortionOfState`, plus FOR PORTION OF bounds in PL/pgSQL trigger variables.
Temporal foreign keys gain ON UPDATE/DELETE CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT, and a later patch adds PERIOD DDL.
author_claims: Trigger firing order follows SQL:2011 15.14 and paper SQL-026R2, and matches DB2 and MariaDB.
A set-returning function for leftovers allows future user-defined types, such as spatial types or multi-dimensional ranges.
READ COMMITTED gives lost updates under concurrency, as MariaDB does, and SELECT FOR UPDATE beforehand avoids them.
RETURNING should omit leftovers, because they represent unchanged data.
Leftover inserts need no INSERT privilege, because they add no new information.
brief.thread_state: Peter Eisentraut committed the core FOR PORTION OF patches in April 2026 for v19, and follow-up bugs (INSTEAD OF views, SRF protocol, BEFORE triggers changing the range) were fixed or closed by July 2026. Nobody reviewed the trigger, foreign key, PL/pgSQL and PERIOD patches in the visible thread.
unclear: The second mail thread attached to the v20 CommitFest entry is not shown, so the exact v20 patch set is unknown.
The CommitFest entry needs a rebase as of 2026-11-09.
Exposing `ForPortionOfState` through `TriggerData` fixes an executor struct as extension API, and the thread does not discuss its stability.
Treating NULL bounds as unbounded was left for user input during beta, and the thread shows no outcome.
`ExecGetAllUpdatedCols` omits the range column, and the thread shows no final fix.
How CASCADE and SET NULL foreign key actions behave under READ COMMITTED, which the author said he would explore.

prior_attempts.title: SQL:2011 application time
prior_attempts.quote: IMO, if this temporal feature is to happen, btree_gist needs to be moved into core first. Having to install an extension in order to use an in-core feature like this isn't going to be an acceptable experience.
prior_attempts.reason: Peter Eisentraut held that btree_gist must move into core first, because the temporal keys need it for most uses. He also objected that the index owns the constraint instead of the reverse, and asked for FOR PORTION OF without triggers. In January 2022 the patch set no longer applied and reviews had unanswered comments, so the entry was set to Waiting on Author.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: Temporal keys shipped in v18, so the btree_gist objection no longer blocks this work. FOR PORTION OF now inserts leftovers through ExecInsert without SPI and was committed for v19. Only the trigger, foreign key action, PL/pgSQL and PERIOD patches remain open.

objections.title: PERIOD DDL adds hidden columns with no dump, psql or catalog story
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs alter table add period and later dumps the database. If pg_dump emits the hidden generated range column as a normal column, the restore creates both the period and a duplicate column. If pg_dump omits the column, a restore into v19 fails on the PERIOD syntax with no fallback.
objections.argument: Message #4 says PERIOD support rests on hidden GENERATED range columns. Postgres has no hidden user columns today, so select *, \d, information_schema.columns, column renames and pg_dump all need a defined rule. The visible thread does not discuss any of these, and nobody reviewed the PERIOD patch. Message #26 drops the patch from the set because it often conflicts, so its design was never checked against these paths.
objections.author_must_show: How do pg_dump, psql \d, information_schema and ALTER TABLE RENAME, DROP and SET DATA TYPE treat the hidden range column behind a PERIOD?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 bases PERIODs on hidden generated range columns, and the visible thread has no review of that patch. Nothing shown says how pg_dump, psql or information_schema treat the hidden column.

objections.title: The FOR PORTION OF column is not tracked as an updated column
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch skips CHECK constraints, generated columns or UPDATE OF triggers based on ExecGetAllUpdatedCols. It never sees the range column that FOR PORTION OF narrows, so a check on valid_at is skipped. Nothing fails until a user reports bad data.
objections.argument: Message #45 showed that ExecGetAllUpdatedCols omits the range column. In message #53 the author proposed a separate bitmapset as the robust fix and a one-line union as a short-term patch, and the thread shows no final choice. The CASCADE and SET NULL patches and the trigger patches add more code that depends on knowing which columns change. Each new user of updated-column sets must remember this special case, and no check fails if a patch forgets it.
objections.author_must_show: Will the range column be added to one updated-columns set that all consumers use, before the trigger and foreign key patches build on it?

critic.reasoning: Message #45 shows ExecGetAllUpdatedCols omits the range column, and message #53 offers two fixes without the thread recording a choice. The foreign key and trigger patches build on this code, so the question applies to them.

objections.title: ForPortionOfState exposed in TriggerData becomes a fixed extension API
objections.failure_scenario: An extension author writes a C audit trigger that reads tg_temporal->fp_targetRange and fp_leftoverstypcache. A later release reshapes ForPortionOfState for PERIODs, user-defined types or multi-dimensional ranges. The extension breaks at the next major upgrade, or misreads the struct if it is not rebuilt.
objections.argument: The patch documents an executor-internal struct in trigger.sgml, including a TypeCacheEntry pointer and a column name string, as the C trigger interface. The thread already plans changes that touch this state: PERIOD support, user-defined leftover functions (message #31), and links from leftovers to the old row (message #21). No message discusses which fields are a stable contract. Once trigger.sgml documents a struct, changing it costs every C trigger that reads it.
objections.author_must_show: Which minimal fields do triggers need, and why not expose those in a small dedicated struct rather than the executor's ForPortionOfState?

critic.reasoning: TriggerData already exposes internal structs, and C extensions are rebuilt for each major version, so breakage on upgrade is normal. But trigger.sgml would document internal fields such as fp_leftoverstypcache, and the thread does not say which fields triggers may rely on.

refuted.title: PL/pgSQL bound variables take a spelling the standard left open
refuted.failure_scenario: Users write audit triggers against the new PL/pgSQL FOR PORTION OF variables. A later SQL standard adds its own trigger syntax for the FROM and TO values with different names or semantics. Postgres must then keep two interfaces, or break the existing triggers.
refuted.argument: Message #1 quotes SQL-026R2, which leaves trigger access to the FOR PORTION OF bounds as a future Language Opportunity. Message #1 also says SQL-language triggers should wait for the standard, but the same caution is not applied to PL/pgSQL or to TriggerData. The proposal does not say whether the variables expose a range value or separate FROM and TO values, or how they will map to PERIODs. Nobody in the visible thread reviewed that design.
refuted.author_must_show: What names and value types do the PL/pgSQL variables use, and how would they coexist with a future standard trigger syntax for these bounds?

critic.reasoning: PL/pgSQL trigger variables are a Postgres-specific interface with no standard counterpart, so a future standard syntax in SQL-language trigger definitions can coexist with them. Message #1 already holds back the SQL-language case for that reason.

refuted.title: NULL bounds may mean different things for range columns and PERIODs
refuted.failure_scenario: A user switches a table from a range column to a PERIOD and keeps the same update ... for portion of ... from null to x statements. If PERIODs reject NULL as message #44 suggests, statements that ran yesterday now raise errors, and the change in meaning shows up only at run time.
refuted.argument: Message #40 questions treating NULL as unbounded, and message #43 defers the choice to feedback during beta. The thread shows no outcome of that feedback. Message #44 then suggests forbidding NULL only for PERIODs, which gives one clause two meanings depending on how the column was declared. The PERIOD patch in this entry is where that choice would become fixed.
refuted.author_must_show: Will FOR PORTION OF treat NULL bounds the same way for PERIODs as for range columns, and what did beta users report?

critic.reasoning: Message #44 only says NULL could be forbidden for PERIODs if the project later wanted that; no patch proposes it. The scenario needs that undecided change plus a user converting a range column to a PERIOD.

refuted.title: tg_temporal exposes an executor struct as trigger API
refuted.failure_scenario: An audit or trigger-based replication extension written in C reads fp_rangeAttno and fp_targetRange from tg_temporal. A later release adds PERIOD support (two columns, no single range attno) or user-defined leftover types and changes ForPortionOfState. The extension then compiles but reads the wrong field, and the error shows up as wrong replicated or audited data, not as a build failure.
refuted.argument: The v52-0007 docs publish ForPortionOfState from nodes/execnodes.h, including an internal TypeCacheEntry pointer, as part of TriggerData. Message #31 and message #4 already plan PERIODs and user-defined types, both of which change what the struct must describe. The commit message names trigger-based replication as a target user, so third-party code will depend on the layout. The thread does not discuss whether the struct is stable or what a trigger may rely on.
refuted.author_must_show: Which fields of ForPortionOfState are promised to trigger authors, and how will PERIOD support change them without silently breaking C triggers?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. Its PERIOD scenario is also weaker, because message #4 builds PERIODs on a hidden range column, so a single range attno still exists.

refuted.title: PERIOD hidden generated columns need a pg_dump and pg_upgrade story
refuted.failure_scenario: A user adds a PERIOD to a table, so a hidden generated range column is stored in the heap. On pg_upgrade, the schema is dumped with --binary-upgrade. If pg_dump emits the hidden column as an ordinary column, or emits the PERIOD and lets it create a new column at a different attnum, the restored catalog no longer matches the old heap files, or the hidden column becomes visible.
refuted.argument: Message #4 describes PERIOD DDL as "based on hidden GENERATED rangetype columns". Message #3 reports ordering problems in ALTER TABLE passes. The visible thread does not say how pg_dump, binary-upgrade attnum preservation, or logical replication column lists treat a hidden column. Message #26 drops the PERIOD patch from the posted set, so nobody reviewed these paths.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a table with a PERIOD round-trip through pg_dump and pg_upgrade --binary-upgrade, keeping the hidden column's attnum and hidden status?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which covers the pg_dump treatment of the hidden column. The binary-upgrade attnum question belongs in the answer to that objection.

refuted.title: PERIOD DDL with hidden generated columns adds ALTER TABLE cost
refuted.failure_scenario: A future ALTER TABLE or NOT NULL patch changes pass ordering or relcache handling. ALTER TABLE ADD PERIOD, which adds a hidden generated range column in the add-columns pass, starts failing or produces a wrong catalog state. The ALTER TABLE patch author does not know periods exist and finds out from a field report or a dump/restore failure.
refuted.argument: The author reports that the PERIOD patch conflicts each time cataloged NOT NULL constraints change, and drops it from series for that reason (messages #2, #26). Message #3 describes an ALTER TABLE failure tied to relcache lifetime that was not root-caused in the visible thread. No reviewer engaged with this patch. A hidden column tied to two user columns is a new kind of object for ALTER, DROP, RENAME, pg_dump and psql to handle.
refuted.author_must_show: How do the hidden range column and the period behave under ALTER TABLE, DROP COLUMN, RENAME and pg_dump, and what makes a later ALTER TABLE change fail loudly if it forgets periods?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the ALTER, RENAME and pg_dump questions. The rest is a guess about future ALTER TABLE patches, and message #4 reports the message #3 failure as fixed.

refuted.title: Trigger access to FOR PORTION OF bounds has no shown users
refuted.failure_scenario: Postgres ships tg_temporal and PL/pgSQL bound variables, and extension and PL authors start to rely on the ForPortionOfState layout. Later the SQL standard defines its own trigger syntax for the FROM and TO values. Postgres must then keep both interfaces, or break triggers that users wrote against the first one.
refuted.argument: The only concrete consumer of tg_temporal in the material is the internal RI CASCADE code (patch 0007 commit message), and that code does not need a public API. User demand is described as "probably useful" for auditing or replication, with one INSTEAD OF example in message #54. Message #1 quotes SQL-026R2, which leaves trigger access to these bounds as a future "Language Opportunity", so the interface would come before the standard defines one. Message #7 calls these follow-on patches nice-to-have.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users today need FOR PORTION OF bounds inside their own C or PL/pgSQL triggers, and why can the RI code not get them without a public field?

critic.reasoning: RI actions are triggers and receive their input through TriggerData, so the field is their normal channel. Message #54 makes INSTEAD OF triggers responsible for leftovers, which they cannot compute without the bounds.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: PERIOD DDL rests on a hidden generated range column that pg_upgrade must carry over.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: Publications publish the UPDATE or DELETE and then one INSERT per temporal leftover.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patches add pg_proc entries, touch pg_constraint helper lookups, and PERIOD DDL needs catalog support.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: `TriggerData` gains `tg_temporal`, which points to the executor's `ForPortionOfState`.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patches add FOR PORTION OF, temporal foreign key actions and PERIOD DDL from SQL:2011, with range columns as an extension.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: The patch touches createplan.c, planner.c and pathnode.c to carry FOR PORTION OF to ModifyTable.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump must dump and restore a PERIOD and its hidden range column.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: psql `\d` needs a rule for showing a PERIOD and its hidden column.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Leftover inserts need no INSERT privilege but still fire INSERT triggers.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The PERIOD patch conflicts each time cataloged NOT NULL constraints change, and the range column is a special case for updated-column sets.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: nodeModifyTable.c gains FOR PORTION OF handling in the UPDATE and DELETE path.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How do pg_dump, pg_upgrade, psql `\d`, information_schema and ALTER TABLE RENAME or DROP COLUMN treat the hidden range column behind a PERIOD?
Will the range column be added to one updated-columns set that all consumers use, before the trigger and foreign key patches build on it?
Which fields of `ForPortionOfState` may C triggers rely on, and why not expose only those in a small dedicated struct?
How do temporal CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT behave under READ COMMITTED when a concurrent session changes the referenced row?
Which patches make up the v20 set in this CommitFest entry, and can each be committed on its own?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut committed the core FOR PORTION OF patches for v19. The follow-on patches need someone who knows the RI trigger code and ALTER TABLE, and nobody reviewed them in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a documented C trigger struct, foreign key actions that depend on FOR PORTION OF bounds, and a hidden-column mechanism for PERIODs across ALTER TABLE, pg_dump and psql, with no end date.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong: the author kept the series going past 50 versions, keeps a wiki page of design decisions, and took part in follow-up bug fixes through July 2026.

priority.reason: The patches complete a standard feature whose core is already committed, for users of temporal tables. They touch RI triggers, PL/pgSQL, ALTER TABLE and pg_dump, so review is costly, and the entry needs a rebase first.

provisional_note: The second mail thread on the CommitFest entry and the code were not read, so the exact v20 patch set is unknown. The foreign key actions' concurrency behaviour and the PERIOD implementation could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Push down time-related SQLValue functions to foreign server
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets postgres_fdw push down current_timestamp, localtimestamp, current_time, localtime and now() by computing them locally and sending the value as a parameter in the remote query. A later version tried to extend this to any stable subexpression without remote Vars.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane asked for a general mechanism instead of a one-off feature for SQLValueFunction: any stable local subexpression of a safe-to-ship type would become a parameter, which means restructuring is_foreign_expr and deparse.c. He rejected the author's prototype because its repeated recursion is probably exponential in expression size. No new version followed, and the entry was returned with feedback after waiting on the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But that may be moot, because I don't think we can tolerate the double-recursion approach you took here.

precedents_retrieved.title: WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING Temporal Tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds SQL:2011 system-versioned temporal tables, keeping current and historical row versions in one table with generated row start and row end timestamp columns. Queries without a system time filter get an implicit filter for current rows, and FOR SYSTEM_TIME clauses query past data.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Vik Fearing, after trying to fix the patch, judged its design too flawed, because it conflates system_time periods with system versioning; ALTER TABLE ADD/DROP SYSTEM VERSIONING adding and removing columns was one example. Earlier review points such as the missing 2201H error for anomalies stayed open. Simon Riggs saw weeks of further work on one of two possible designs, had no plans to continue, and suggested Return with Feedback. The patch also no longer applied.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The design decisions are just too flawed, and it conflates system_time
periods with system versioning which is very wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: When tuple_update() or tuple_delete() finds a concurrently updated tuple in read committed mode, the table AM locks the updated version itself instead of returning TM_Updated for a separate tuple_lock() call. Later versions also had update and delete return the old tuple through a slot passed by the executor, which avoids refetching it and helps table AMs with costly TID lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Version 15 was committed in March 2023, then reverted after Andres Freund's post-commit review. He showed that RETURNING could use the wrong tuple, with an isolation test that fails. He also criticised the new API: the ignored wait parameter, tmfd turned into an input, and the LazyTupleTableSlot code. The redesigned old-tuple API came days before the version 16 feature freeze, and he said it was not ready for 16. In March 2024 the author planned to push a revised version, and the visible messages do not show why the entry was finally returned with feedback in October 2024.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I guess this really is part of my issue with this change - it optimizes the rare case, while not addressing the same inefficiency in the common case.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL:2011 application time
precedents_retrieved.summary: Four patches add SQL:2011 application time: PERIODs, temporal primary key and unique constraints with WITHOUT OVERLAPS, UPDATE/DELETE FOR PORTION OF, and temporal foreign keys. Range columns are accepted wherever the standard accepts a PERIOD, and temporal keys are built on exclusion constraints with GiST indexes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut held that btree_gist must move into core first, because the temporal keys need it for most uses. He also objected that the index owns the constraint instead of the reverse, and asked for FOR PORTION OF without triggers. In January 2022 the patch set no longer applied and reviews had unanswered comments, so the entry was set to Waiting on Author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMO, if this temporal feature is to happen, btree_gist needs to be moved
into core first.  Having to install an extension in order to use an
in-core feature like this isn't going to be an acceptable experience.

precedents_retrieved.title: Re: BUG #18741: Detaching a partition referencing a partitioned table fails with a trigger-related error
precedents_retrieved.summary: Alexander Lakhin reported that detaching a partition fails with an internal trigger error when the partition has a foreign key to a partitioned table and its new parent has no matching foreign key. Tender Wang and jian he discussed fixing this, mainly by rejecting such ATTACH PARTITION commands except where the partition references a non-partitioned table or its own parent's hierarchy.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They contain the bug report and two design suggestions with no patch, review or decision, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: TimestampTz->Text->TimestampTz casting fails with DateStyle 'Postgres'
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes timestamptz input treat "LMT" as a noise word by adding it to datetktbl[] as IGNORE_DTF. This lets values printed with DateStyle 'Postgres' for dates before a zone's first standard offset be read back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier and Tom Lane objected that LMT is a time zone abbreviation, so ignoring it in the date/time keyword table is wrong; it should map to the GMT offset LMT has in the session time zone. Tom Lane then showed the problem is wider, because abbreviations such as MMT can be read back with a different meaning than TZDB gives them, and moved the discussion to a separate -hackers thread. The author closed the entry, calling the patch wrong and saying the issue needs more discussion.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We should be mapping it to whatever GMT offset "LMT" means
in the selected zone (assuming there is an entry, which it seems like
there is in most of them).

precedents_retrieved.title: BRIN bloom and multi-minmax indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds two BRIN opclass families: bloom filter summaries for equality searches, and multi-minmax summaries that keep a list of min/max intervals per range so the index still works when correlation degrades. It also changes bringetbitmap() to pass all scan keys to the consistent function at once and, in later versions, depends on the separate opclass parameters patch for settings such as false_positive_rate and values_per_range.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The series stopped applying because it was built on the opclass parameters patch, which commit 773df883e broke. The author left that fix to the opclass parameters thread, and no rebased version appeared for about two months. Michael Paquier then marked the entry Returned with feedback. The shown messages contain no design objection that decided the outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This has been close to two months now, so I have the patch as RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: POC: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes tuple_update() and tuple_delete() lock a concurrently updated tuple as soon as they detect it, so a separate tuple_lock() call before the read committed recheck is no longer needed. It also simplifies nodeModifyTable.c and removes an extra table_tuple_fetch_row_version() call in ExecUpdate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message, from the author on 2022-07-29, said a benchmark showed a small, noisy gain and that he would bring the patch into a more acceptable shape. No later message appears before the entry was returned with feedback.

This commit reverts 137805f89 as well as the associated commits 015e88942,
5306df283, and 68d704edb.  We found multiple bugs in this feature, and

requires a considerable rewrite, which may or may not be possible to
accomplish in time for beta2.  In my judgment reviewing the rewrite will
be easier to accomplish starting from a clean slate, so let's temporarily
revert what's there now.  This also leaves us in a safe state if it turns
out to be necessary to postpone the rewrite to the next development cycle.

roaster_notes.note: The only close precedent is [P7], and its recorded reason (btree_gist must be in core first) was resolved before temporal keys shipped in v18. Its other points, index ownership and FOR PORTION OF without triggers, were addressed by the committed v19 design. [P1] (revert over empty ranges) and [P3] (system versioning) record reasons that do not apply to the remaining v20 patches.
The core FOR PORTION OF syntax, RETURNING, row count and trigger order were settled and committed in v19, so this review does not reopen them.

The committed FOR PORTION OF core adds no WAL records or on-disk format change, and leftovers are published as ordinary INSERTs. The pg_range columns were settled in message #29. Both objections cover only the uncommitted follow-on patches.

The one privilege decision is that leftover inserts need no INSERT privilege and still fire INSERT triggers. That rule is in the core patches committed for v19, is documented with a SECURITY DEFINER warning, and is covered by privileges tests. The remaining v20 patches are the TriggerData field, PL/pgSQL variables, temporal FK CASCADE/SET NULL/SET DEFAULT and PERIOD DDL. The FK actions run through the existing RI trigger path, so they follow current cascade practice for the executing role and for RLS, and the other patches add no new privilege or exposure. Not checked: whether INSERT row-level security policies apply to leftover rows. The visible thread does not discuss it, and it belongs to the committed core rather than this entry.
Peter Eisentraut is engaged and committed the core FOR PORTION OF patches. The objections cover only the remaining v20 patches.

The core FOR PORTION OF patches were committed for v19, and Postgres has no other way to get what the remaining patches add. For a DELETE, a trigger cannot recover the FOR PORTION OF bounds from OLD, NEW or transition tables, so neither user triggers nor temporal CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT can be built outside core today. PERIOD DDL may overlap with a plain range column, but it is the standard form, and I cannot confirm that a stored generated range column covers all its uses.
The CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT actions and the PERIOD DDL complete standard SQL:2011 features that DB2 and MariaDB already implement, so I do not raise a demand objection against them.
